newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Unthinkable" not to correct deficits - Trichet.
newsitem.headline: "Unthinkable" not to correct deficits - Trichet.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet told afternoon daily Le Monde it would be unthinkable not to take corrective measures on public deficits.
Trichet referred to an OECD report which predicted all EU countries except Greece, Italy, Germany and France heading for public deficit levels of three percent or less of GDP in 1997.
Setting Greece aside, he said of Italy, Germany and France: "These three countries will naturally take corrective measures. Not taking corrective action is unthinkable".
Asked what would happen if France's public deficit hit 3.5 percent of GDP, Trichet was quoted as saying, "Such a figure would make France the worst performer in the European Union apart from Greece".

He said delaying the euro was legally inconceivable because it would require amending the Maastricht Treaty. Any delay would amount to "taking the enormous risk of a de facto annulment of the treaty".
"I do not believe it for a second," he said, adding that he saw the euro being put in place on January 1, 1999.
"That's what (new Socialist prime minister) Mr Jospin said and I fully share his sentiment," Trichet added.
